card.name: Words before a verb of starting or causing
card.fires_on: A word right before the verb that says something starts, is stirred up, or is brought about (arise, foment, take hold, begin, put in power). It is usually a subject or adverb, in web text about conflict, rights or disease.

modes.label: Subject before an onset verb
modes.description: A noun that is about to be followed by a verb of arising, starting or taking hold.
modes.example: changes the way an<< infection>> takes hold, which may benefit the mouse

modes.label: Adverb or particle before a causing verb
modes.description: A small word such as to, soon or usually that comes just before a verb of stirring up, starting or bringing about.
modes.example: foment resentment against the government of the Republic of Vietnam and<< to>> proselitize their fellow prisoners

modes.label: Words about oppression or intolerance
modes.description: A word in text about oppression or hostility, just before the verb for being directed at or taken away.
modes.example: Future seminars will deal with other specific groups against whom<< intolerance>> is directed in many parts of the world

card.writes: It seems to push the next word toward mount/inc-type verbs of starting or setting up, such as mounting.
card.plain: It marks the spot just before a verb saying that something starts, arises or is stirred up.
